name: BAC Credomatic
why_it_matters: Regional bank acquirer: BAC's FY2025 results deck claims market leadership in Central American credit cards with a 53% acquirer share by transaction volume (Q3 2025) and 40% issuer share, and says payments through BAC equal 55% of regional GDP; the only group able to process both acquiring and issuing for Visa, Mastercard and Amex across the region.

name: Tilopay
why_it_matters: Costa Rica-born gateway claiming 65K+ affiliated businesses, 33 markets, 1.4M+ successful transactions per year and 47 partner banks; accepts cards, SINPE Movil, Apple Pay/Google Pay and BAC Tasa Cero / Minicuotas / Credix installment programs.

name: PlacetoPay (Evertec)
why_it_matters: Evertec's gateway already operating in Colombia, Ecuador and Costa Rica when it launched in Panama in April 2021; multi-channel (web, social, QR, IVR), PCI DSS, Evertec 3DS and Scudo fraud tools. No public merchant figure found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator whose Costa Rica docs list cards (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Diners, Discover, JCB, with recurring and refunds), SINPE bank transfer (min 1,000 CRC, USD charging) and SINPE Movil (min 10 CRC); CRC settlement with optional USD charge.

name: Local Payment
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP offering SINPE virtual-account pay-ins in CRC and USD (codes 1420/1421, synchronous push, 24h, real-time notification) plus SINPE and SINPE Movil payouts; no cards shown on the Costa Rica page.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: EBANX launched Costa Rica operations in March 2021; its current 'more markets' page shows only Visa, Mastercard and Amex cards for Costa Rica (no local APMs) and gives no share figure.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Credit cards 68% and debit cards 16% of Costa Rican e-commerce (PCMI 2024, cited in ICEX e-Pais April 2025); e-commerce reached USD 6.4B in 2024. Installments run through issuer programs (BAC Tasa Cero, Minicuotas, Credix) exposed by gateways such as Tilopay.

name: SINPE Movil
why_it_matters: BCCR's mobile instant-transfer rail: 4.52M subscribers made 747.51M transactions worth CRC 12.53 trillion in 2025 (BCCR data via Semanario Universidad); from Sep 2025 e-invoices carry a dedicated code to measure SINPE Movil as a payment method at merchants.

name: SINPE (bank transfer)
why_it_matters: Interbank transfer over BCCR's SINPE network; offered by dLocal as 'Sinpe' bank transfer (min 1,000 CRC, 5-day expiry, USD charging) and by Local Payment as SINPE virtual accounts. No public e-commerce share figure found.

name: Banco Nacional (cash / online banking)
why_it_matters: Banco Nacional cash and online-banking collection is the local non-card option shown on PayRetailers' and Nuvei's Costa Rica coverage; no public share figure found and cards already cover 84% of e-commerce (PCMI 2024).

name: Telered
why_it_matters: Panama's domestic transaction switch ('la autopista transaccional de Panama', 35 years): operates Sistema Clave (national debit network, e-Clave for online), ACH Directo and ACH Xpress instant transfers; counters on its site show no published volumes.

name: BAC Credomatic
why_it_matters: Regional bank acquirer: BAC's FY2025 results deck claims market leadership in Central American credit cards with a 53% acquirer share by transaction volume (Q3 2025) and 40% issuer share, and says payments through BAC equal 55% of regional GDP; the only group able to process both acquiring and issuing for Visa, Mastercard and Amex across the region.

name: PagueloFacil
why_it_matters: Panamanian online payment gateway (APIs, SDKs, plugins, dashboard) accepting credit/debit cards, Tarjeta Clave and PagoCash; registered by the Superintendencia de Bancos as payment-instrument and e-money issuer (Res. 00096-2025); clients named include Nespresso, Planet Fitness, Digicel and Air Panama. Pricing 3.5% + $0.50 per approved transaction.

name: Tilopay
why_it_matters: Entered Panama in April 2025 with 1,200 Panamanian businesses (25,000+ regionally); accepts Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Yappy, Tafi and CLAVE and claims to be the only gateway enabling Yappy transactions.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator offering cards (Visa/Mastercard credit and debit, Amex, Discover, JCB; recurring and refunds) plus Punto Pago cash kiosks and PayCash in USD; dLocal added Panama in Oct 2020 together with Tarjeta Clave.

name: Nuvei
why_it_matters: Panama is listed among Nuvei's local acquiring countries in Latin America and Nuvei offers Clave (cards, e-wallet) through its platform; no public volume figure.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: ICEX e-Pais (Nov 2024): cards, credit and debit (especially Visa and Mastercard), are the most used e-commerce payment method in Panama, with online sales projected at USD 1,173M in 2024; PCMI data cited there show debit overtook cash as preferred method in 2024. No public e-commerce share split found.

name: Tarjeta Clave
why_it_matters: Telered's national debit network; when dLocal added Panama (Oct 2020) it described Tarjeta Clave as 'among the primary payment methods in Panama'; supported by Nuvei, PagueloFacil and Tilopay. No public share figure found.

name: Yappy
why_it_matters: Banco General's payment app: 1.8M+ registered clients (over 60% of adults), about 70M transactions per month of which 18% are merchant payments, and 36K+ businesses collecting with Yappy (La Prensa, Aug 2026); merchants integrate the Boton de Pago Yappy from a Yappy Comercial account (merchant ID + secret key).
typical_access: direct (Boton de Pago Yappy) | via Tilopay

name: Nequi Panama
why_it_matters: Banistmo's 100% digital bank/wallet, named with Yappy by ICEX (Nov 2024) as 'ganando terreno rapidamente' in e-commerce; no public user or share figure found.

name: ACH Xpress (Telered)
why_it_matters: Telered's instant interbank transfer (seconds, 24/7) and Xpress by phone number; ICEX notes bank transfers are common in Panamanian e-commerce. No e-commerce share figure found and no aggregator coverage confirmed.

name: Punto Pago
why_it_matters: Cash collection through Punto Pago payment kiosks in Panama, offered by dLocal (7-day expiry, immediate notification, refunds); PayCash is the alternative cash network. No public share figure found.

name: AZUL
why_it_matters: Grupo Popular's acquiring brand (Servicios Digitales Popular, launched 2014) with hosted payment page, API, recurring billing, cardholder authentication and data vault; accepts Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, Diners, tPago and Altice wallet; Click to Pay with passkeys live at 9,000+ merchants (Apr 2026), first acquirer in the region per Mastercard.

name: CardNET
why_it_matters: Consorcio de Tarjetas Dominicanas, bank-owned acquirer/processor with 25+ years, online solutions, the ATH ATM network and ACH transfers; elDinero (2015) ranked it among the 20 largest merchant acquirers in Latin America. No recent public volume figure.

name: VisaNet Dominicana
why_it_matters: Third local card acquirer, partnered with Banco Vimenca and the La Nacional and Cibao savings associations (elDinero, 2015); no recent public figures found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator offering DOP cards (Visa/Mastercard credit and debit with recurring, Diners, Discover; min 10 DOP) and Banco Popular cash tickets (DIRECT and REDIRECT flows).

name: Pagadito
why_it_matters: Non-bank domestic PSP headquartered in El Salvador with coverage of 13 countries including this one; claims 10,000+ affiliated merchants, PCI DSS Level 1, and offers payment button, links, QR, recurring charges and tokenization.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: EBANX went live in the Dominican Republic in 2021; its current coverage page shows Visa, Mastercard and Amex cards only for the country, no local APMs and no share figure.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: PCMI (Mar 2025): credit cards 66% and debit 21% of e-commerce sales volume; market USD 5.2B in 2024. BCRD: card operations rose from 229.7M (2021) to 432.1M (2025). No installment practice documented in sources found.

name: tPago
why_it_matters: Local mobile wallet: PCMI (2025) says PayPal (58%) and tPago (40%) make up wallet-based e-commerce volume, with wallets at 7% of total; accepted by AZUL. No current tPago user figure found (older reports cite 300K+ users).

name: PayPal
why_it_matters: PCMI (2025): PayPal is the largest wallet in Dominican e-commerce with 58% of wallet volume (wallets 7% of total); listed by AZUL among online payment options.

name: Pagos al Instante (BCRD)
why_it_matters: BCRD's instant payment service settled 43.3M operations in 2025 (from 11.1M in 2021); ACH/direct transfers reached 360.9M operations in 2025 (revista Mercado, Oct 2026). Bank transfers are 4% of e-commerce volume (PCMI 2025); no aggregator coverage confirmed.

name: Banco Popular (cash)
why_it_matters: Cash ticket payable at Banco Popular, offered by dLocal (min 10 DOP, 5-day expiry); cash is only about 1% of e-commerce volume (PCMI 2025).

name: Datafast
why_it_matters: Self-described leading payment network in Ecuador ('lider en Red de Puntos de Pago'), 60,000+ devices in 24 provinces; e-commerce via Dataweb payment button, mobile SDK, recurring payments, tokenized one-click and WooCommerce/Magento/PrestaShop plugins; offers 'pagos en diferido' (installments). No public market share found.

name: Medianet
why_it_matters: Second major card network (Datafast, Medianet and AustroRed are the three largest), with Web Checkout, Boton de Pagos, payment links, QR Cobro and cart plugins; EMIS reports net sales +10.15% in 2025. No public market share found.

name: Kushki
why_it_matters: Ecuador-born PSP positioning itself as LatAm's non-bank regional acquirer (acquiring licences in Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Chile); Ecuador docs cover cards with OTP/3DS, recurring and one-click with 'diferidos' by BIN, bank transfers, cash points, Smartlinks and Shopify/VTEX plugins.

name: PlacetoPay (Evertec)
why_it_matters: Evertec acquired Colombia-based PlacetoPay to strengthen Colombia and Ecuador; by April 2021 it operated in Colombia, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Panama. No public Ecuador merchant figure found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator offering USD cards (Visa/Mastercard credit and debit, Amex and local brand Alia, all with recurring), Pago Efectivo cash tickets and the Deuna wallet (redirect, 720-minute expiry).

name: PayRetailers
why_it_matters: Ecuador market page lists Visa/Mastercard, online banking via Banco Pichincha and Banco Guayaquil, and a wide cash network (Pichincha, Guayaquil, Western Union, Farmacias Economicas, Medicity, Mi Comisariato, cooperatives); cites USD 11.31B digital payments market (no year).

name: Nuvei
why_it_matters: Ecuador is among Nuvei's local acquiring countries; local methods named are bank transfers via Banco Pichincha, Banco Guayaquil and Banco Bolivariano, plus Western Union (Activa) cash.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: CECE/UEES e-commerce study 2024: 55% of online purchases paid with credit cards and 44% with debit (prepaid under 1%), e-commerce USD 4,618M (+22%). Installments ('diferido con y sin intereses') are standard: Datafast offers deferred payments and Kushki exposes diferido options by BIN; Alia is a local card brand.
typical_access: direct | via dLocal, Kushki, Nuvei, PayRetailers, EBANX

name: Deuna
why_it_matters: Banco Pichincha's wallet, described as Ecuador's largest digital payments ecosystem: 5 million clients and 420,000 affiliated merchants (Vistazo, Dec 2024); CECE notes wallet use in e-commerce is still marginal. dLocal offers Deuna as a redirect wallet.

name: PayPhone
why_it_matters: Ecuadorian wallet plus merchant gateway (payment button, links, QR, API): 600,000 active users and 50,000+ merchants on Payphone Business (Jul 2025); card acquiring fee 5% + VAT. No aggregator coverage confirmed.

name: Bank transfer (Banco Pichincha / Banco Guayaquil online banking)
why_it_matters: Online-banking transfers through Pichincha, Guayaquil and Bolivariano are offered by Nuvei and PayRetailers; CECE says transfers are common but not measured in its 2024 card-based shares. No public share figure found.

name: Pago Efectivo (cash voucher)
why_it_matters: Cash ticket offered by dLocal in Ecuador (min USD 1, 5-day expiry); Western Union and bank-counter cash are offered by Nuvei and PayRetailers. No public share figure found; CECE does not measure cash in its card-based mix.

name: BAC Credomatic
why_it_matters: Regional bank acquirer: BAC's FY2025 results deck claims market leadership in Central American credit cards with a 53% acquirer share by transaction volume (Q3 2025) and 40% issuer share, and says payments through BAC equal 55% of regional GDP; the only group able to process both acquiring and issuing for Visa, Mastercard and Amex across the region. In El Salvador its Compra Click e-commerce platform had 1,500+ merchants by 2020.

name: Pagadito
why_it_matters: Non-bank domestic PSP headquartered in El Salvador with coverage of 13 countries including this one; claims 10,000+ affiliated merchants, PCI DSS Level 1, and offers payment button, links, QR, recurring charges and tokenization. Headquartered in El Salvador.

name: Serfinsa
why_it_matters: Salvadoran paytech operating 25,000+ payment points, ~900 ATMs and 24M+ transactions a year (2022); runs QuickPay, an interoperable QR ecosystem with Bancoagricola, Abank, Davivienda, Hipotecario, Opto, Chivo Wallet and NIU; expanding to Central America.

name: n1co
why_it_matters: Fintech from the Hugo founders: 10,000+ businesses use its gateways in El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala and it passed 1M monthly transactions in El Salvador (Jun 2023); cards, payment links, QR, consumer account with Visa debit.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator offering USD cards (Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex, Discover, Diners; recurring and refunds) plus PuntoXpress and Akipago cash vouchers.

name: PayU
why_it_matters: PayU announced expansion to Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Costa Rica in Dec 2022, processing cards in USD and local currencies with 3DS 2.0 and ML risk tools; no volume figure.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Dollarized market where BAC Credomatic is the dominant acquirer (53% Central America); dLocal supports six card brands with recurring. No public e-commerce share figure found (PCMI data library covers El Salvador but figures are paywalled).

name: Transfer365
why_it_matters: BCR's free 24/7 instant transfer system (since Jun 2021) channels 88.7% of interbank transfers; ~3.6M operations in Jan 2025 and 68M+ cumulative operations to Jan 2025; Transfer365 Movil had 69.3% acceptance in the 2025 financial inclusion survey. No aggregator pay-in coverage confirmed.

name: PuntoXpress
why_it_matters: Cash collection network with 1,250+ points in all 14 departments (Walmart, Super Selectos, Farmacias San Nicolas, Texaco, Pollo Campestre); dLocal offers PuntoXpress vouchers (min USD 1.5, 5-day expiry). No public share figure found.

name: Akipago
why_it_matters: Cash voucher payable at pharmacies, gas stations and stores, offered by dLocal (min USD 1, 5-day expiry); no public share figure found.

name: NeoNet (ex-VisaNet Guatemala)
why_it_matters: ICEX (Dec 2025) calls it 'la principal empresa de medios de pago locales'; Visa/Mastercard-backed with 11 partner banks (BAM, BAC, CHN, Banrural, Ficohsa, G&T, Industrial, Promerica, Interbanco, Cuscatlan, Multicredit); e-commerce via NeoLink, NeoPay, NeoPagos recurring and CyberSource; NeoCuotas 2-18 month 0% installments.

name: BAC Credomatic
why_it_matters: Regional bank acquirer: BAC's FY2025 results deck claims market leadership in Central American credit cards with a 53% acquirer share by transaction volume (Q3 2025) and 40% issuer share, and says payments through BAC equal 55% of regional GDP; the only group able to process both acquiring and issuing for Visa, Mastercard and Amex across the region. ICEX lists VisaNet and BAC Credomatic as the most used card platforms in Guatemala.

name: QPayPro
why_it_matters: Local PSP that integrates with the NeoNet and BAC Credomatic processors to accept online card payments (ICEX 2025); Shopify app available. No public volume figure.

name: Pagadito
why_it_matters: Non-bank domestic PSP headquartered in El Salvador with coverage of 13 countries including this one; claims 10,000+ affiliated merchants, PCI DSS Level 1, and offers payment button, links, QR, recurring charges and tokenization. ICEX notes regional platforms such as Pagadito have gained ground for agile online-store integration.

name: Tilopay
why_it_matters: Regional fintech gateway that ICEX says gained relevance in Guatemala in 2024-2025 with optimized checkout; payment links, QR and e-commerce integration.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator offering GTQ cards (8 brands incl. Amex, Diners, Discover, JCB; recurring, chargebacks), PayCash cash tickets and the SoyFRI mobile wallet (redirect, GTQ 10,000 daily limit); 13-digit CUI required.

name: Local Payment
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP offering GTQ pay-ins via SoyFri QR, Wallet Fri (GTQ 1-10,000, real-time) and Akisi online referenced payments (GTQ 20-7,500, T+1), plus IFT/ACH payouts.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: PCMI 2024 (cited by ICEX Dec 2025): internationally-enabled credit cards 63% and debit cards 14% of e-commerce; 80% of volume is mobile. Installments via NeoCuotas (2-18 months, 0%) and BAC programs; high-value purchases financed on BAC, Banrural and G&T cards.

name: Bank transfer
why_it_matters: Bank transfers were 18% of Guatemalan e-commerce in 2024 (PCMI via ICEX), the second method after credit cards; QR and instant transfers popularized in 2024-2025. Referenced-payment access exists via Local Payment (Akisi).

name: Fri (SoyFri) QR wallet
why_it_matters: Wallet on Guatemala's standardized interoperable QR regulated by Banco de Guatemala, linking bank and cooperative accounts (G&T, Banrural, Promerica, Micoope; Banco Industrial and BAC currently excluded); digital wallets were 3% of e-commerce in 2024 (PCMI via ICEX).

name: PayCash
why_it_matters: Cash ticket payable at commercial chains and banks, offered by dLocal (min 1 GTQ, 5-day expiry); Nuvei names Banco de Antigua and Caja Desarrollo cash networks. 'Other' methods incl. cash on delivery were only 2% of e-commerce in 2024 (PCMI via ICEX).

name: BAC Credomatic
why_it_matters: Regional bank acquirer: BAC's FY2025 results deck claims market leadership in Central American credit cards with a 53% acquirer share by transaction volume (Q3 2025) and 40% issuer share, and says payments through BAC equal 55% of regional GDP; the only group able to process both acquiring and issuing for Visa, Mastercard and Amex across the region.

name: Pagadito
why_it_matters: Non-bank domestic PSP headquartered in El Salvador with coverage of 13 countries including this one; claims 10,000+ affiliated merchants, PCI DSS Level 1, and offers payment button, links, QR, recurring charges and tokenization.

name: n1co
why_it_matters: Salvadoran fintech with operations in Honduras; 10,000+ businesses on its gateways across El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala (Jun 2023); cards, payment links and QR.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator: Honduras docs list HNL cards only (Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex, Discover, Diners; recurring and chargebacks); dLocal's market page sizes e-commerce at USD 2.15B (Statista 2024) with 17.1% CAGR to 2025.

name: PayU
why_it_matters: PayU's Dec 2022 Central America expansion covers Honduras, processing cards in USD and HNL with 3DS 2.0 and anti-fraud tools; no volume figure.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: No reliable public e-commerce share found (a vendor guide cites ~45% cards, unsourced). CNBS counted 102,485 POS terminals at Dec 2024 (+11.1%); La Prensa (Dec 2025) reports card and transfer payments spreading in shops while many customers still prefer cash.

name: Tigo Money
why_it_matters: Honduras' main mobile-money wallet (with Tengo, per CNBS); already over 1 million users and ~2M transactions a month in 2016 (La Prensa); no recent public figure found. No aggregator pay-in coverage confirmed.

name: Cash on delivery
why_it_matters: Cash remains the default for many Honduran shoppers: a merchant quoted by La Prensa (Dec 2025) says 80% of customers still prefer cash, though 'few businesses still charge only in cash'; no formal e-commerce share figure found.

name: Bank transfer (ACH Pronto)
why_it_matters: ACH Pronto is the interbank transfer network (used by Local Payment for HNL payouts, T+1); La Prensa notes electronic transfers are increasingly accepted at merchants. No e-commerce pay-in aggregator confirmed and no share figure found.

name: BAC Credomatic
why_it_matters: Regional bank acquirer: BAC's FY2025 results deck claims market leadership in Central American credit cards with a 53% acquirer share by transaction volume (Q3 2025) and 40% issuer share, and says payments through BAC equal 55% of regional GDP; the only group able to process both acquiring and issuing for Visa, Mastercard and Amex across the region.

name: Pagadito
why_it_matters: Non-bank domestic PSP headquartered in El Salvador with coverage of 13 countries including this one; claims 10,000+ affiliated merchants, PCI DSS Level 1, and offers payment button, links, QR, recurring charges and tokenization.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator offering NIO cards (Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex, Discover, Diners; recurring and chargebacks) and PuntoXpress cash tickets (min 1.5 NIO, 5-day expiry).

name: Cards
why_it_matters: BCN Q4 2025: 3.6M payment cards in circulation (+16.7%), debit the most used instrument with 34.4M transactions in the quarter. Since 1 Jan 2025 all card payments settled in Nicaragua must be in cordobas (BCN circular); purchases at foreign online merchants are shown in USD with customer choice of currency.

name: PuntoXpress
why_it_matters: PuntoXpress operates a cash collection network in Nicaragua (and El Salvador); dLocal offers PuntoXpress cash vouchers in NIO. No public share figure found.

name: Banpro Billetera Movil (bank wallets)
why_it_matters: BCN counts 892,834 digital-wallet users (+14%) and 478,806 e-money accounts (+18.6%) at Q4 2025 without a brand split; Banpro's Billetera Movil is one of the bank wallets. No e-commerce share figure and no aggregator coverage found.

name: ATC Red Enlace
why_it_matters: ASFI-supervised operator of Bolivia's largest electronic payments network with a published acquiring contract, PCI DSS certification, online collection products ('Enlazate Online', 'cobrar por Internet en mi tienda virtual') and recent American Express acceptance. No public volume figure.

name: Linkser
why_it_matters: Santa Cruz-based card administrator acting in both issuer and acquirer roles for Visa, Mastercard and proprietary cards; merchant acquiring with digital onboarding and 'Tienda virtual' via Marketlink; annual reports through 2025. No public volume figure.

name: PagosNet
why_it_matters: Bolivian collection platform ('Cobra con tarjeta, QR o efectivo'); EBANX names PagosNet as its Bolivia local method alongside cards. No public figures found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator offering BOB cards (Visa/Mastercard credit and debit; no recurring), QR payments (immediate notification), bank transfer, Pago al Paso and Multipago cash, and 'Domiciliate' recurring QR; CI or NIT document required.

name: Local Payment
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP offering QR Bolivia pay-ins (code 1150, BOB 1 to 1,000,000, real-time notification, 24h) plus bank transfer and wallet payouts (Tigo Money, Yape).

name: QR BCB (QR Simple)
why_it_matters: Bolivia's interoperable state QR: BCB reports 892M QR operations in 2025 (vs 385M in 2024) worth Bs 357,747M, and QR at 36% of payments vs cash 64% (from 15/85 in 2020); Asoban: QR is 94% of interbank electronic transfer orders, 3.7M users and 1.5M merchants.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Visa and Mastercard credit and debit acquired through ATC Red Enlace and Linkser; dLocal supports BOB cards but without recurring. No public e-commerce share figure found; cash is still 64% of payments (BCB 2025).

name: Tigo Money
why_it_matters: Bolivia's main mobile wallet with over 1 million users (May 2023), partnered with e-commerce marketplace elGenioX (5% discount for wallet payments) and with Red Enlace; Local Payment lists it for payouts only, no pay-in aggregator confirmed.

name: Pago al Paso
why_it_matters: Cash ticket network offered by dLocal (with Multipago as alternative; min 1 BOB, 5-day expiry) in a market where cash was still 64% of payments in 2025 (BCB). No public e-commerce share figure.

name: Bancard
why_it_matters: Paraguay's main card-acceptance network: 100,000+ merchants, 100M+ monthly transactions and 4.5M+ cards processed (site); e-commerce via vPOS, QR and the Zimple wallet; Bancard Report: online hit 5M transactions in Aug 2026 (2x YoY) with debit at 75% of online operations.

name: Procard
why_it_matters: Second card processor (26 years, 90+ member entities, 30,000+ adhered merchants) for Unica Debito, Visa, Mastercard and Credicard programs; no e-commerce product described on its site.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator with the widest APM set: PYG cards (Visa credit without recurring; debit chargeable in USD), Infonet, Practipago and Wepa cash, Zimple, Tigo Money, Billetera Personal and Wally wallets, QR payments and bank transfer; min PYG 7,500.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: EBANX launched Paraguay in 2021; its coverage page lists credit, debit and prepaid cards for Paraguay, no local wallets or cash, and no share figure.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Bancard Report (Sep 2026): debit cards are 75% of online operations and debit transactions grew 157% through Aug 2026; e-commerce reached 5M transactions in August 2026. dLocal supports charging debit cards in USD. No installment share found.

name: QR Bancard (interoperable QR)
why_it_matters: Bancard QR passed 180M transactions in 2025 (~20M in December) and a record 25M in Aug 2026 (+53% YoY); the BCP added a central QR interoperability module to the payment system and a QR e-commerce product was rolled out beyond its pilot.

name: SPI instant transfers (SIPAP)
why_it_matters: BCP's instant payment system (2023) with aliases: ~379M operations projected for 2025 (327% of GDP), alias transfers 58.1M through Oct 2025 (8x YoY); per-operation cap raised to G. 10M in Mar 2026. Available through dLocal's bank transfer method.

name: Tigo Money
why_it_matters: Largest mobile wallet: over 1 million monthly users and 60-65% of e-money (Apr 2024); interoperable with banks via SIPAP and with Bancard QR at 70,000+ merchants; offered by dLocal as a redirect wallet.

name: Zimple
why_it_matters: Bancard-linked wallet connected to the financial system, accepted at 29,000+ merchants with Infonet POS and cash-out at 1,000+ Infonet ATMs (4% transfer fee); offered by dLocal. No user figure published.

name: Infonet (cash)
why_it_matters: Bancard's Infonet collection network (100,000+ merchants accepting digital payments per Bancard); dLocal offers Infonet, Practipago and Wepa cash tickets (min PYG 7,500, 5-day expiry). No public e-commerce cash share found.
